text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Greek Prime Minister Kostas Simitis yesterday denied rumours that the Mediterranean countries of the EU do not support the integration efforts of Central European countries, following a visit to Prime Minister Gyula Horn's office. @

- Sandor Czirjak and Frigyes Harshegyi are expected to formally announce their resignations as National Bank vice presidents today in wake of an internal investigation which discovered that the Bank has lost over HUF3 billion through a major professional mistake.
- The US credit-rating institution Standard & Poor has upgraded Hungary's creditworthiness to BBB- from BB+, which means "recommended for investment".
- Six members of the panel of directors of the IMF have arrived to Hungary for a three-day visit. @

- At the congress of the Federation of European Journalists, Prime Minister Gyula Horn, Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs and Young Democrat leader Viktor Orban presented arguments in favour of EU expansion.
- Ivan Szabo, leader of the People's Party, announced Monday that his party has submitted a draft resolution to have Parliament declare solidarity with the people of Tibet.
- The Polus Centre due to open in Budapest on November 8, will be Eastern Europe's largest shopping, entertainment and service facility, reporters were told yesterday. @
- Opel Bank Hungary Rt. is to launch a new loan scheme named "Flex Loan" for the purchase of second-hand Opel cars.
- Two hand grenades went off in one minute outside the Komjadi swimming pool in Budapest's Second District early Monday, about 24 hours after a similar blast occurred in downtown Erzsebet ter.
NEPSZAVA
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy and his Danish counterpart Mogens Lykketoft conferred on ways of promoting economic and financial ties in Budapest Monday. @

- The Central Crime Fighting Directorate sequestered lawyer Marta Tocsik's tangible assets Monday morning, while the lawyer said she would appeal to the Capital's Court to confirm the validity of her contract with the State Privatisation and Holding Co.
- Hungarian-born actor Tony Curtis was among several people awarded the Pro Cultura Hungarica award in Parliament yesterday.
NEPSZABADSAG @
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky are expected to formally open a gas pipeline connecting Gyor with Baumgarten.
- The economic cabinet will work out the details of its monetary policy according to a projected figure of 18 per cent inflation.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @

- Hungarian and Slovak legal representatives will meet in New York with president of the International Court of Justice on November 4 to agree on the order of the verbal proceedings due to start on February 17, 1997, regarding the dispute over the Gabcikovo Dam.
- The National Bank of Hungary reduced its repo rates by 0.25 per cent on Monday.
- The plastics manufacturer Pannonplast recorded a 77 per cent after-tax profit increase in the first three quarters of this year.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
